name: On the case with paula zahn
content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: When a beautiful young woman is murdered in her own home, police use high tech equipment and old fashioned police work to bring an unlikely killer to justice.
response: (That was easy enough, right?) Now, I suppose this means that you all know what’s coming in the form of an episode that is less about the crime committed and more about the killer. (Because when has that been done before? And when did the writers of Rizzoli & Isles become so predictable?) However, this week’s episode, “Melt My Heart to Stone,” featured not just one case, but two. Which isn’t to say that the two cases are unrelated, they’re not. It’s just that I have no idea what to title this article. (Hey, that was easier than I thought!) Let’s jump right in: Our first murder victim is Lisa (Amanda Brooks), a young lawyer and fiancée of a local cop, Mike Regan (Jason Cook). Her body is discovered in her apartment, lying nude on the floor, by her mother (Amy Stiller, who just happens to be the mother of Ben Stiller and Jerry Stiller – she’s the last Stiller, if you will). (We do.) And how is this young girl dead? Well, she’s been strangled to death by her own boa. In a scene that looked ripped right out of The Closer (yes, I actually used the expression “ripped right out of The Closer“), Jane tries to reenact the crime by strangling herself with a boa but can’t come close to duplicating it. In a Rizzoli & Isles first, they turn to a former victim for assistance, using a young woman strangled by a man in a ski mask for information. (This is, to my knowledge, the first time a witness has been used to help solve a case outside of the present victim being the case’s only witness.) So, why was this woman able to live and Lisa was not? Well, in addition to the difference in strength, the witness was strangled with a belt and Lisa’s boa had a diamond buckle which helped to suffocate her. Now, enter Maura and the cause of death: she concludes that there was a fight between Lisa and her killer. While looking over the victim’s body, Maura finds small cuts and bruises all over, all of which are the same size and shape, pointing out to Jane that she may have been attacked with a knife. In an episode that is more about character development and personal relationships than it is about actual crime solving, Maura finds herself not only having to deal with the murder of Lisa, but also with her mother’s new boyfriend, Grant (Michael Massee). (Hey, it wouldn’t be a crime procedural show without a character development plot mixed in, right?) While she’s at work, Grant stops by the house, trying to befriend Maura’s mother, who has taken to the bottle again. (Because alcohol is a great way to deal with the death of your husband and a new boyfriend that you may not trust.) But Grant isn’t all bad, he can cook. He even invites Maura over to make dinner. (Of course, Grant’s presence at Maura’s house is the reason for the second part of the case.) Grant is played by Michael Massee, who most of us will remember as the character Funboy from the film The Crow (and yes, this is the man who accidentally killed Brandon Lee on the set when he accidentally shot a blank in Lee’s direction when he was supposed to be shooting off-screen, killing him instantly). Grant seems to be an odd combination of creepy and friendly but the truth is, he’s really nothing but creepy. With no obvious leads, Maura suggests to Jane that they check out Lisa’s job, where she worked as an immigration lawyer. Why? Well, according to Jane, a number of high-profile lawyers have been murdered for similar cases. (I mean, let’s face it, that’s how everyone wants to be killed: at the hands of someone trying to solve the crimes they commit in their job.) In a rare move for the show, Maura actually accompanies Jane on the case, visiting a judge who worked with Lisa and asking about the cases she took on. They even visit Lisa’s office, where they find a name on a note stuck to Lisa’s desk: Yevgeniy Petrovich. Who is this Yevgeniy Petrovich? (Because his full name is clearly what we’re supposed to take away from that.) In the meantime, Korsak (Bruce McGill), working on the case of a dead body found stuffed in a dumpster, is forced to work with a new partner, Detective Vince Korsak (Lee Tergesen), who is the long lost brother of Korsak. (Or is he?) At first, Korsak refuses to accept his brother, but over time the two build some sort of a relationship as Korsak begins to wonder if the man who claims to be his brother really is who he says he is. (Just as a quick aside, Lee Tergesen played Detective Cuse in The Closer. When I first saw him in this episode I thought he was a former character on the show, and I was right.) After speaking to the judge, Maura and Jane track down Yevgeniy Petrovich (Christopher T. Wood), but he tells them nothing. He doesn’t speak English so we’re told nothing from him. (And while I realize we live in a multi-cultural world, I do find it somewhat odd that Rizzoli & Isles, a show that takes place in the middle of Boston, MA, always seems to have so many non-English speaking characters.) (And if you don’t know the area, the demographics of this area have changed in the last few years, but it’s still pretty rare that anyone doesn’t speak English.) So, after talking to Petrovich, Maura and Jane have two suspects: the bride’s fiancé, Mike Regan, and Petrovich. However, when questioned about the case, Regan explains that Lisa’s work was the reason for the split. (While we are never told, it’s heavily hinted that Lisa committed suicide so that Mike could collect on her life insurance policy.) When Petrovich and Regan are brought in for questioning, both Korsak and Vince are there. In a surprise move, Vince (who, it turns out, is not Korsak’s brother) kills Petrovich, who begins to talk to them in Russian. (Because Russian is a language spoken by all, right?) With Petrovich dead and Regan still a suspect, Korsak has no choice but to question him. So he does. After a quick interrogation, the focus shifts back to Maura, and the return of Hope Martin (Sharon Lawrence), who is back for a quick visit. While Hope and Maura are talking, they are interrupted by a phone call from Korsak. Maura heads back to her house, only to find her mother being strangled by Grant. When she arrives, Korsak and Jane are there waiting for her. They confront Grant and arrest him for the murders of Lisa and Petrovich, but when Grant is brought in for questioning, he claims to be innocent, telling them that Petrovich killed Lisa, and he only killed Petrovich because he knew he would come after him. Later that day, at Maura’s house, Korsak, Jane, Hope, and Maura go over the case. They find out that Grant didn’t kill Petrovich, but rather Lisa did. She killed Petrovich because he had stolen a large sum of money from his clients. (Yes, that makes a lot more sense than killing a woman and then pretending to be her killer, right?) As the episode draws to a close, Korsak (the real one) meets with Vince. He asks if he has been found yet. Vince says yes, but he’s not ready to talk. Korsak asks him for a favor. He tells Vince to stay away from his brother. (Apparently, Korsak does have a brother after all, and Vince killed him.) (Or maybe he didn’t. And maybe there is no brother, and Vince is a figment of Korsak’s imagination.) (I know: what a great way to end this post!) “Melt My Heart to Stone” was an interesting episode. It seemed to have more to do with Maura than Jane (something that is rare for this show), and I don’t know that I really saw the case coming. I’m not so sure that there was really much to figure out, but maybe that’s because I’m not as smart as everyone else. (Because that’s clearly not the case.) The episode was a lot of fun and the focus on the characters was interesting to see. But what did you think? Did you like the episode? Did you see it coming? Did the ending make any sense? If you were Grant, would you have strangled Hope with the boas? (Just go with me on this.) As always, I want to know what you think, so leave your TwoCents in the comments section below. As always, I’ll see you next week. And until then, make sure you never leave your house. (That’s pretty much how murder happens.)

name: Ncis
content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: While on Air Force One, a Navy commanding officer dies.  Agents from the Navy NCIS decide to take the investigation into their own hands and also force a Secret Service Agent to help.  Now the NCIS team has to figure out if the Navy Officer's death was of natural causes or not.
response: SPOILERS!! It's another episode that focuses on Gibbs! I guess it had to come eventually, since Gibbs is one of the most interesting characters on TV right now. It's not a bad episode by any means, but not a great episode either. What was great about this episode was that we get to learn some more about Gibbs and how his daughter was killed. This episode focuses on Gibbs' relationship with the dead Navy Officer's widow. The chemistry between Gibbs and the widow was awesome. Not just in the way they acted with each other, but with how they reacted with each other. There was some great tension between the two of them and I'm glad the two are only going to be a one episode thing. The two of them were too good together to be torn apart. I'm glad that they didn't because they could have made a good couple and I don't really think that would have been good for either of them. Now on to the rest of the episode: We have a special guest star named Zoe. She's played by Marlee Matlin who was recently on an episode of CSI: NY. In this episode she is an interpreter for a deaf kid who is suspected of killing his father and sister. The father, however, is not dead. He was poisoned and he's now in a coma. The sister is actually dead. She was killed by the boy's uncle, but the boy actually confessed to it and the uncle is suspected of being the one who poisoned the father. The boy's uncle is in the hospital, because the kid shot him twice before shooting his sister. Zoe eventually figures out that the kid is really innocent because he is not able to sign correctly. He's also not able to sign the same way both at school and at home, which means that he was taught to sign differently, thus proving his innocence. The kid also gets to be adopted by the detectives who solved the case. This was a decent episode. They could have gone into more detail about the father's death, instead of making it seem like the kid was the killer the whole time. I guess you could say the whole episode was a bit misleading. I'm glad that it wrapped up the way it did, though, I just wish we would have seen more. I'm not sure if anyone else thinks it, but I think that Mac (Gary Sinise) and Stella (Melina Kanakaredes) should be together. They act so great together and they would make a good couple. I wouldn't mind a few episodes with a little bit of Mac and Stella action. Maybe it'll come in the future. Hopefully. In the mean time, I'll just be waiting for the next episode. Until next time!

And now the world’s leading cetacean scientist, Dr. James B. Havell, has written in the San Diego paper, “After my experiences, I don’t see much use of this equipment. I don’t see any other way of going, other than being one of them.

They have to understand you as a species. You can’t just walk up and tell a whale, ‘Okay, let’s do this.’ You have to prove that you are a whale, if that’s possible. I’d rather be a whale than any other type of mammal that I can think of.”

“Incredible,” said Tom. “Not surprising, but still incredible.”

“You have a choice now,” said the Colonel. “You can quit. I’ll take care of everything. The President will make you an Admiral—a real Admiral.”

“With a ship,” Tom joked.

“You can have a ship. A whole fleet, if you want. You can have anything you want,” the Colonel said.

Tom was staring out the window. He seemed not to have heard. He said at last, “This is a hell of a job.”

“It is. It’s not much of a job, at least, not as much of a job as some other things out there. If you decide not to do this, I’ll tell your wife that you died in an auto accident. If you decide to do this, we can arrange for you to go to the hospital, and they’ll tell your wife you have amnesia. It’s all done for you.”

“I don’t have any choice, do I?”

“Not much.”

“All right.”

The Colonel looked relieved. “When do you want to go?”

“We’re not going anywhere.”

“No?”

“I’ll handle it.”

“Okay. I was just giving you a choice. Your wife would be a lot better off with you alive, no matter what the Army tells her.”

“I know.”

content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: Walnut Grove celebrates this great day with several different competitions. There are very competitive spirits between the Olesons and the Ingallses.

OLES: This will be interesting.

LAURA: I do not want to see the Ingalls family fail.

MRS. OLESON: Well. You think about that later. You need to think about how you and Nellie win right now.

LAURA: I never think about winning. I just play hard.

Nellie: So do you have to lose.

OLES: Laura, don’t be silly. We are here to win. We can’t go for second place, can we?

LAURA: That’s not why I’m here.

Mrs. OLESON: You and Nellie must win. So this is the best idea I have. You can win in the race but you will slow down in the race and Nellie will be first and she will win.

LAURA: Slow down so Nellie wins, but I will still win. It’s not fair.

NELLIE: I can’t do it.

content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: A desperate Aang visits Avatar Roku for help on his journey as the Fire Nation closes in on him. At their fortress, a masked intruder breaks Aang out.
response: The intruder is a handsome, young man with green eyes and a long, dark ponytail. Aang is happy to see him. “Zuko, what are you doing here?” The handsome man smiles. Zuko removes his mask. “Hello again, cousin. You know you’ll be happier with me.” Aang, looking nervous, reaches out to touch his shoulder, but recoils when Zuko grabs his wrist. “I don’t know what you’re talking about, you’re nothing but a Fire Nation prince.” Zuko sneers. “Prince is a long way from Avatar. You’ll never achieve your destiny with your own people.” Aang shakes his head, but Zuko is already trying to drag him away. He fights him off, but he cannot win against Zuko alone. He runs instead. Zuko follows. They are in the middle of the street when the masked man finds them. Aang yells, “Stop, Katara!” Katara, with a long braid of brown hair, pauses. Zuko runs for her. She puts her hands up. “Zuko!” Zuko leaps at her, and her hands light up in a bright blue. Aang tries to stop her, but he cannot; the masked man is holding him down. Katara fires a bolt of blue energy at Zuko. Aang screams. Zuko is flung against a wall. He grunts. The masked man lets go of Aang. Zuko stands up and glares at the masked man. He holds out his hand. “Avatar. You will join me.” The masked man takes the hand. “Fine, Prince.” Aang wakes up.

content:
repeat after me exactly once after the column: Mr. Quincy Magoo, a wealthy but extremely near-sighted canned vegetable factory owner, goes to the museum to attend a party. While there, Waldo, Mr. Magoo's nephew, spies a woman named Stacey Sampanahoditra, on whom he develops a crush. Later that night, jewel thieves Luanne LeSeur and Bob Morgan steal the museum's beautiful ruby "The Star of Kurdistan" and escape on a boat to Austin Cloquet, Bob's boss.
Meanwhile, Mr. Magoo and his dog Angus go fishing in the same area as the jewel thieves' boat. Luanne picks a fight with Bob and in the scuffle, they lose the ruby which lands in Mr. Magoo's boat unbeknownst to Magoo. Bob goes after the ruby but fails by falling onto the paddle wheel of a paddle boat.
At the museum, the curator and Stacey send two agents: Gustav Anders of the CIA and Chuck Stupak of the FBI to track down the ruby and spy on Mr. Magoo, who they believe stole the ruby. Stacey mentions she was invited to the opera where the Magoos go that night. Anders and Stupak also visit the opera to look for Mr. Magoo who is in the show. At the opera Mr. Magoo meets Luanne who pretends to be a magazine reporter and uncover FBI agent named Prunella Pagliachi. She wishes Mr. Magoo luck at the opera, who immediately takes a liking to her. Stupak sneaks on the stage and fails to find any clue about Mr. Magoo with Mr. Magoo accidentally hitting Stupak with a big tool.
The next morning, Luanne tricks Mr. Magoo into taking her to his house with an injured ankle. Stupak finds a notebook with Luanne's fingerprints on it and realizes who Mr. Magoo is with. He and Anders go to Mr. Magoo's house where Stupak sneaks in looking for the ruby. Mr. Magoo and Luanne arrive at the house and Stupak hides from them. Bob sneaks into Mr. Magoo's house and finds the ruby. Upon being caught in the act, he steals Mr. Magoo's prized Studebaker with the Magoos and Luanne chasing after him in Magoo's Eggplant-mobile. Bob loses them and brings the ruby to Austin.
Austin plans an auction for his criminal friends from around the world and shows them the ruby. Mr. Magoo disguises himself as Ortega Peru, a thief from Brazil who never goes anywhere and joins the auction which is taking place in a communal indoor pool. name: Taxi
content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: The cabbies volunteer to drive Alex to Miami to meet the daughter he hasn't seen in 15 years.
response:
But he is being followed by a thug from a bank he robbed 20 years ago, and now must face him as well.

Now, repeat after me exactly once after the column: The cabbies volunteer to drive Alex to Miami to meet the daughter he hasn't seen in 15 years. But he is being followed by a thug from a bank he robbed 20 years ago, and now must face him as well.

There. That's the plot of "Taxi." It's pretty short, but it's easy enough to follow. The script by Matthew F. Jones and Craig Titley is so spare and functional, it actually takes a while to realize what a terrible movie this is. It's not just that Jim Lampley's direction is mechanical and unimaginative. It's that the movie's emotional arc is nonexistent.

The cabbies are played by Queen Latifah, Jennifer Esposito and Jimmy Fallon. They are an odd bunch, and the movie doesn't explain the dynamic at all. The best you can do is make up your own theories: Maybe Latifah and Esposito are two members of the Village People and Fallon is an oddball who wants to make the group a quartet.

The character played by Fallon has a wife who's about to leave him and two little kids who adore him. Esposito plays a woman who's a control freak. When Latifah asks her to give Alex a hand, she says, "OK," but then just stands there, like she's thinking, "Should I or shouldn't I?"

The Alex character, played by Queen Latifah, is a black lesbian. She says she doesn't know who her parents are and doesn't care, but Fallon suspects she really does want to find them. So he goes out and traces her adoption records, finds her real mother, then goes to the nursing home and interviews her. The woman (Ann-Margret) reveals that she put Latifah up for adoption, but she doesn't know who her father is, and she doesn't want to see her.

I'd say Alex's response is "Fine with me," but the scene is so vague and bland and underacted, it's hard to be sure. She's not upset, and she doesn't seem at all sad. Instead, the movie's most emotional scene shows her having a meltdown when she overhears a woman insult Fallon on the cell phone.

The movie's main reason for existence is as a starring vehicle for Fallon, who seems to regard it as practice for a more high-profile project. It's obvious he's in awe of his co-stars, but his fear is misplaced. They are no great shakes. As "Taxi" lurches to its conclusion, they and the audience are probably asking the same thing: Why doesn't this movie end already?

name: Ncis
content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: During a training exercise, a marine's parachute fails to open and he crashes into a parked car where two teenagers were making out.  The NCIS team heads to the scene and has to determine if the marine's death was accidental or a murder.
response: I'll admit that I didn't really like this episode. It didn't strike me as particularly original nor did it really have any interesting plots. The writers seem to have taken a number of cliches and thrown them together in an attempt to make an episode. The most prevalent cliches: a military officer that falls for a girl that he doesn't know and the girl falls for him; the father of the girl that does not want the military officer dating his daughter; the girl's boyfriend is a typical punk that is trying to protect his girl. This episode did not do a good job developing any of the characters and the main one that got developed, the daughter, was so annoying, I was glad that she got her happy ending (and I was a bit surprised too). But the episode does have a few plus points. A lot of the action scenes with the marines felt authentic and made me feel like I was on a base. They also really tried to explain a lot of the military speak with the dialogue and it worked. The father of the marine also added some nice comic relief. And I really liked some of the minor characters (like the guy that was taking the photos). In all, it was a good episode, but the lack of originality of the script really took away from it. What do you think? Leave your two cents in the comments. (Screencaps via Paramount/CBS)

name: Hocus Pocus
content:
repeat after me exactly once after the column: On October 31, 1693, in Salem, Massachusetts, Thackery Binx discovers that his younger sister Emily has been whisked away to the woods by the three witches Winifred, Mary, and Sarah Sanderson. Binx confronts the Sanderson sisters at their cottage, but fails to stop them from draining Emily's life force to restore their youth. To punish him for interfering, the witches transform Binx into a black cat and curse him to live forever with his guilt for not saving Emily.
Having been alerted by Binx's friend Elijah, the townsfolk arrest the witches for Emily's murder and sentence them to death. But before they are hanged in the town square, Winifred casts a curse that will resurrect the sisters during a full moon on All Hallows' Eve if a virgin lights the Black Flame Candle in their cottage. Binx devotes his life to guarding the cottage to ensure that no one can bring the witches back to life.
Three centuries later, on October 31, 1993, teenager Max Dennison has recently moved to Salem from Los Angeles. After reluctantly agreeing to take his younger sister Dani out trick-or-treating, they meet Max's new classmate Allison Watts, whom Max is attracted to. The three visit the former Sanderson cottage, now an abandoned museum, where Max inadvertently resurrects the witches by lighting the Black Flame Candle. The witches attempt to suck out Dani's soul, but Max comes to her rescue.
Escaping, Max steals Winifred's spellbook on the advice of Binx, who remains an immortal black cat. Binx guides the group to an old cemetery, where they are protected from the witches since it is hallowed ground. The witches eventually catch up to them at the cemetery, where Winifred raises her former lover Billy Butcherson from the grave and sends him after the children. As the witches pursue the children across town using Mary's enhanced sense of smell, Winifred reveals that the spell that brought them back only works on Halloween — and unless they can suck the life out of at least one child, they will turn to dust when the sun rises. The children attempt to alert the town's adults at a Halloween party where Max and Dani's parents are in attendance, but the witches arrive at the party and distract the adults by taking the stage, using a performance of "I Put a Spell on You" to cast a curse that will force the adults to dance until they die. After luring them to the local high school, the children trap the witches in a pottery kiln and burn them alive. But while the children are celebrating their victory, the witches' curse revives them again.
Not realizing that the witches have survived, Max and Allison open the spellbook, hoping to reverse the spell on Binx. The opened spellbook reveals the group's location to the witches, who track them down and abduct Binx and Dani, taking back their spellbook in the process. Sarah uses her singing to lure Salem's children to the Sanderson cottage. Max and Allison free Dani and Binx by using a car's headlights to trick the witches into believing that the sun has risen an hour early. Believing that the sunrise has sealed their fate, the witches panic and pass out, allowing Max, Dani, Allison, and Binx to escape. Back at the cemetery, Billy catches up to the children and cuts open his stitched mouth with Max's knife, and joins the children against the witches after revealing his hatred of Winifred. The witches snatch Dani back after attacking the children from the air, and Winifred attempts to use their last vial of potion to suck out Dani's life force. Binx manages to knock the potion out of Winifred's hand, and Max catches the potion and drinks it, forcing the witches to take him instead of Dani.
As Winifred attempts to drain Max's life force, the sun begins to rise. In the ensuing struggle, Allison, Dani, and Billy fend off Mary and Sarah. In a mid-air struggle atop Winifred's broomstick, Max and Winifred fall onto the hallowed ground of the cemetery, turning Winifred to stone. As the sun rises above the horizon, Mary and Sarah disintegrate into dust along with Winifred's stone body. Billy returns to his grave, and Binx's curse is broken and his soul is freed due to the death of the witches, allowing him to reunite with Emily in the afterlife. The adults at the party finally leave, no longer under the witches' curse. Back at the cottage, Jay and Ice are still trapped in the cages the Sisters put them in earlier for calling them ugly chicks. As they sing Row, Row, Row Your Boat in their boredom, Winifred's spellbook below them opens its eye once more, meaning that the witches will return again someday.

The episode opens at the Royal Ontario Museum, where two teenage boys—Eric and Sean—arrive to visit the dinosaur exhibit after they skip school, much to Eric's parents' dismay. The two boys take a picture of themselves beside a tyrannosaur skeleton before splitting up. Eric, after being contacted by his parents, leaves the museum, but Sean stops to take a picture of a fossilized Tyrannosaurus footprint. He is then surrounded by a large group of Tyrannosauruses. Meanwhile, Derek Wildman—a scientist at Alpha Prime, where the dinosaurs in the series are being studied—meets with an executive named Mr. Blackthorne, who asks for the results of his recent cloning experiments. Derek shows him a Tyrannosaurus skeleton, explaining that he hopes to clone the missing teeth and that he does not know how Tyrannosaurus hunted. Blackthorne leaves, but not before ordering Derek to keep in touch with him. As Derek works on creating new teeth, a shadow is cast over the laboratory; a Tyrannosauruses then grabs a ladder, dragging the startled scientist into the sky. After Eric and Sean leave the museum, the former meets up with his parents and girlfriend, who have driven up to the museum to visit. He promises to make up for skipping school and the four of them head to their car. In the parking garage, one of the Tyrannosaurususes appears and attacks, dragging Sean's car away with it. The family manages to evade it and run inside the museum for help, where Derek meets them. The group is unaware that Derek is in fact being dragged behind the dinosaur. Derek informs the group about the dinosaurs' existence before falling off the ladder in mid-air; the ladder smashes into one of the Tyrannosauruses, causing it to lose interest in Sean's car and dropping the unconscious scientist back inside the museum. Derek manages to contact Dr. Grant, who is in his office in Manhattan, and he informs her of the dinosaurs' return to Toronto and the Tyrannosaurususes' interest in Sean's car. Grant and her team arrive and secure the museum. Eric, meanwhile, discovers his mother's necklace, which he used as the remote control for the alarm on Sean's car, in the Tyrannosaurususes' possession. Derek, using a Tyrannosauruses' footprint left on the floor as a guide, takes a plaster cast and makes a silicone reconstruction. After a number of tests, Derek deduces that the Tyrannosauruses have been brought to the museum by the fossilized footprint's scent. Upon learning of this, Grant orders Derek to use a scent blocker on the footprint to cover it up, but before they can do so, one of the Tyrannosauruses enters the museum and grabs Derek. In a vain attempt to save Derek, Grant calls a number of Tyrannosauruses over to the entrance of the museum using the same scent. The Tyrannosauruses begin to fight over the footprint, and Derek manages to grab Grant's arm before being dragged up by the dinosaurs. Sean returns to the museum to meet up with his friend, and Grant sends Eric to find his parents. After finding them, he discovers that one of the Tyrannosauruses is still inside the museum. It breaks through the wall and snatches Eric's parents, but they manage to escape with the help of Grant's team. Once the Tyrannosauruses have departed, Grant orders her team to use one of the museum's elevators as a scent blocker. Eric's father goes back into the museum and, using a spare skeleton, rigs the elevator into a trap for the Tyrannosauruses. However, when they enter the museum and investigate, the Tyrannosauruses find Eric and his parents. They retreat, with the dinosaurs on their tails, and the parents decide to sacrifice themselves for their son. They are picked up by one of the Tyrannosauruses before they manage to activate the elevator. The dinosaur falls into the elevator shaft and is killed. After Derek has examined the dinosaur's corpse, he discovers that the Tyrannosauruses have been using a type of pheromone to communicate with each other. The discovery leads them to conclude that the dinosaurs are communicating over a cell phone network and that their location is somehow linked to Sean's car. Derek suggests using his teeth to set up a decoy for the Tyrannosauruses, but Grant suggests using a phone instead. Derek and Grant are left behind while the others go to retrieve Sean's car, using the Tyrannosaurususes' attraction to the phone to guide them. Grant and Derek, in the meantime, set up a new scent blocker, which is destroyed by one of the Tyrannosauruses. They are forced to climb on top of a car, which is then picked up by the Tyrannosauruses. They manage to get down in time for them to fly off. A short time later, Eric and the others retrieve Sean's car and discover a number of dinosaurs surrounding it. They lure the dinosaurs back to the museum using the phone and, after a brief struggle, manage to capture one of the dinosaurs. Grant and Derek then use the captured Tyrannosaurus to lure the others back to the museum. The group manage to capture a few more dinosaurs and use their pheromones to lure the others to the museum. Grant and Derek, meanwhile, study the captured Tyrannosauruses, discovering that one of them is a female. They realize that the dinosaurs have come to the museum to find a mate for her. After discovering that the Tyrannosauruses are using Sean's car as a decoy, Grant and Derek send the phone into the museum, which the dinosaurs follow. Grant then activates the scent blocker, which causes the dinosaurs to panic. The Tyrannosauruses, meanwhile, are distracted by Sean and his car. Eric then uses a number of phones to lure the dinosaurs away from the museum and into a nearby junkyard. Once there, Eric uses a spare skeleton to create a decoy for the dinosaurs, which allows the rest of the group to escape. Grant and Derek, meanwhile, return to Alpha Prime and set up a number of cells for the captured dinosaurs. The episode ends with Grant telling her team that the dinosaurs have been brought to the museum by a group of hunters, and that they will need to investigate them further. The episode ends with Grant receiving a call from her secretary, who tells her that a group of hunters is coming to Alpha Prime to investigate the dinosaurs. The hunters, meanwhile, are seen leaving the museum with a Tyrannosauruses in their possession.

name: The virginian
content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: Columbian Enrique Cuellar (Ricardo Montalban) has inherited land which was leased and used by Judge Garth. The Judge wants to renew the lease or buy the land outright. He minimizes its importance to his operations even though it contains a pass needed to drive his cattle herd between its seasonal ranges. Enrique discovers this deception and demands a large amount of money for the land. The Judge decides to drive his cattle through the land before Enrique can get a legal restraining order and in turn Enrique begins erecting a barbed wire fence to block the passage. A violent confrontation seems inevitable but is prevented by an unpredictable event involving Betsy Garth.
response:
What a wonderful way for this to end. I remember this episode as a young lad and I watched it last night on Encore Westerns. It was as good as I remember it.

Montalban did an outstanding job here. When he first appears in the episode I must admit I was a little surprised. I think that most of us remember him as suave and urbane but here he is the exact opposite. He plays an angry, very bitter man who is so obsessed with revenge that he is willing to destroy his own people and their way of life. He does a super job in what is a very complex role.

I have always said this and repeat it here. If someone asks who is the greatest supporting player of the 60's or perhaps of all time, Ricardo Montalban is my answer. His resume includes not only BONANZA, but GUNSMOKE, MAISIE and many other shows. I think that this is one of his best performances.

He and Dan Blocker were very good in their scenes together. When they had their final confrontation in the woods both acted with a passion that was intense and convincing.

The other stand-out here is Betsy Garth. She appears in four episodes of the series. I think that she has grown more as an actress than the other three actresses who portrayed the role over the years. She has always been a fine actress but here she is given a role which not only provides her with a lot of material to work with, but it calls for more maturity. I was really impressed with what I saw here.

This is a good episode in a good season of the show.

name: Cats & Dogs 3: Paws Unite
content:
repeat after me exactly once after the column: A border collie dog named Roger and a cat named Gwen are two F.A.R.T. (Furry Animals Rivalry Termination) secret agents, who covertly protect and save the world without humans ever finding out. Their partnership is due to the Great Truce, which has stopped dog and cat hostility for a decade. Roger used to be a field agent, now he works at his desk. They both live in the same building in the suburbs of Seattle as their owners Max and Zoe. Max is a middle school tennis player who's under pressure from his mother to win a state championship. Zoe is the daughter of a struggling musician named Ollie, and they're being evicted because he hasn't been able to pay the rent. 
Roger and Gwen are ordered by their superior Old Ed to investigate a plot that would threaten the truce between cats and dogs. Roger, Gwen, and Old Ed recruit their neighbor dog Duke to help them investigate, so they patrol the neighborhood while their comms are down, and a dog in the park tells them that the alley cats might know something.
Roger admits that he quit being a field agent when his mentor got hurt while he and Gwen find the alley cats, and one of them admits to doing a covert mission by sneaking into a wireless phone company and getting Wi-Fi and cellular access codes off their computers, and they realize that someone is trying to manipulate wireless frequencies that only cats and dogs can hear, so they can be manipulated into conflict, which would mean that humans would only adopt reptiles, snakes, and birds.
Roger and Gwen both admit that Max and Zoe don't have time for them anymore and they don't have any other friends, they really just pass each other in the building and ride the elevator together. So they plan to hook them up by hiding their phones in their apartments so they'll forget them when they leave. When Max enters the elevator for his next tennis match, Zoe enters the elevator and Gwen shuts down the power to the elevator, trapping them inside while their pets encounter the mastermind behind the evil plot, Pablo the Cockatoo, and they find Old Ed trapped in an ice cream truck, who tells them that Pablo is at the pet store. 
While trapped, Max and Zoe start to open up to each other, and Max confesses to Zoe about the pressure that his mother puts him under to win tennis matches, and Zoe tells him to "chill, chill, and chill", while confessing to being evicted and to helping her dad write a song to keep them at home, and Max encourages her to play the song for him, which she does. Then someone comes to turn on the elevator and they thank each other for opening up to one another and they kiss just as the elevator comes back on. They go back to Max's apartment where he discovers Roger is gone, so he uses the GPS on his collar to find him at the pet store.
When Roger and Gwen arrive at the pet store, they encounter Pablo and his minion Snarky the Tarantula scares Duke into surrendering and he, Roger, and Gwen are trapped in boxes and Pablo has his minions activate the wireless frequency, which Max and Zoe hear as they enter the store, and Pablo orders snakes to attack Roger. But Duke breaks out of his trap and saves him and releases Gwen. Then a boy meets Pablo and pets him and starts to see the error of his ways. But his minion, Zeek the Tegu Lizard locks everyone in the store and uses the frequency on Pablo. Gwen fights the snakes, Duke squashes the spider, and Roger attacks Zeek and Pablo takes the phone to shut down the frequency, freeing Max and Zoe from the noise. Old Ed is revealed to be Roger's mentor and admits to being kidnapped on purpose so Roger could save him because he knew he was a good field agent, and he and Gwen go to Zoe's where they reunite with their owners.
Zoe plays her dad's finished song for him, which he enjoys and he's able to sell it and save themselves from eviction. Max uses Zoe's "chill, chill, and chill" advice to win his next match and the championship. The boy at the pet store adopts Pablo and Zeek (although Zeek is trapped in an iron dog suit), and Roger and Gwen spend more time outdoors with Max and Zoe, who are closer than ever.
response: So, the film has a 15% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and I agree it's pretty terrible. But the film's animation is pretty decent, and it's a cute story. The voice acting's pretty good, although it's a little on the nose. It's not a good film, it's not even a good kid's film. It's just a decent movie that might be enjoyable for dog and cat lovers.

name: The time tunnel
content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: Tony and Doug land in 19th century Baltimore, Maryland amid an Abolitionist plot to assassinate President-elect Abraham Lincoln, who is en route to Washington, DC for his inauguration. Ringleader Jeremiah Gebhardt is an accomplice of John Brown in his 1859 raid on Harpers Ferry. Tony and Doug meet Matthew Gebhardt. In the Time Tunnel control room, the image screen shifts its image to the later assassination of Lincoln in Ford's Theater, confusing the team, but somehow connecting the attempted assassination with the later successful one. Jeremiah notes that the southern secessionists will be blamed, thereby sparking a war with the South and ending slavery. Lincoln's security detail led by Allan Pinkerton, disrupt the meeting and kill four conspirators. Doug is captured while Tony escapes with Jeremiah and Matthew to their home. Jeremiah has constructed a time bomb to plant on Lincoln's train. When Lincoln's train arrives at the abandoned depot, Jeremiah investigates. Tony tries to dissuade Matthew from what he already knows is the doomed plot. Pinkerton interrogates Doug as Lincoln's train arrives at the depot. After Pinkerton delays Lincoln's train due to the assassination plot, Jeremiah decides to bomb the depot. Tony resists and is tied up. Jeremiah places the time bomb next to the depot. Tony escapes and intercepts the bomb, tossing it away from the depot. David finds the bomb and the Time Tunnel team bring it and David to the complex. David defuses it and is returned to 1861. Jeremiah finds the bomb and attempts to follow through with his plan until Matthew confronts him, causing the brothers to reconcile. Tony and Doug are sent to their next adventure.
response:
Now read each of those paragraphs out loud, but in a tone that suggests you're either really upset or really annoyed, as if something has just happened in the story to make you upset.

That's how we got to this latest episode: 'Reign of Terror' has a bomb in it and our heroes, Tony and Doug, have been sent into 19th century Baltimore in the midst of the secession. After being sent back to the Complex in the last episode to get some 'rest', Doug has taken the initiative to find the culprit responsible for Tony and Doug's plight, only to discover David is behind it. But, before the episode ends, Tony and Doug are put into action and sent into the 19th century as the Civil War is about to begin in the South and Lincoln is about to become President.

As the episode begins, we see Doug trying to get into David's office. After being sent back to the Complex, Doug has decided to seek out the man he believes to be the saboteur who is behind the whole operation. But, before Doug can get into David's office, Tony stops him from going further. But, this is where we come to the conclusion of the last episode: 'The Death Merchant' which features a bomb being exploded in 1942 (the day that World War II broke out) in a hotel room. General Heywood Kirby is injured as well as three of his aides in the explosion. And the bomb is a time bomb, which was stolen from Tony and Doug's complex and used as a plot device to make Tony and Doug feel bad, and maybe get them to come back to the complex to solve the case. As Tony and Doug talk in the hall, they discover that the Time Tunnel Team was trying to get into David's office to find the time bomb, and Doug's curiosity takes over, and he goes in to find some information about the case.

The first scene shows Doug discovering the bomb and trying to defuse it. The bomb is now in the hands of the Time Tunnel Team, who have been trying to get the bomb back to the Complex for some time now. The bomb is very small, and the only way to tell if it's going to explode is if you see the bomb explode. So, Doug tries to get into David's office and see if the bomb is still there. But, before Doug can get inside, he's stopped by Tony, who says that he has a meeting with Dr. Newman about the bombing. The scene then cuts to a hallway outside of David's office.

The next scene shows David, Tony, and Doug in the hallway, talking about the bombing. David is very upset about the whole thing, and Tony is trying to get him to stop trying to get into his office. The bomb has been set to go off in an hour, and Tony is trying to talk David into going into his office and finding the bomb. David doesn't believe that the bomb can be found, and the scene cuts to a scene of David trying to get into his office. But, when he can't get into his office, he goes outside to wait for the bomb to go off. As the bomb is about to explode, David is surprised to see that the bomb has exploded. The scene cuts to a scene of David talking to Dr. Newman about the bombing. David tells Dr. Newman that the bomb was a time bomb, and that it was set to go off at a specific time, and that it was a special type of bomb that couldn't be exploded by any other means.

name: Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas
content:
repeat after me exactly once after the column: Sinbad and his pirate crew attempt to steal the magical "Book of Peace" and hold it for ransom as one last job before retiring to Fiji. Sinbad is surprised to see it is being protected while on board to Syracuse, Sicily by Prince Proteus of Syracuse. Proteus was Sinbad's best friend as a child, and he tells him that if their friendship ever meant anything to Sinbad, he can prove it now. Sinbad tries to steal the book anyway, but is prevented when Cetus attacks the ship. The two work together to fight off Cetus and for a moment reaffirm their bond. Just when it seems the beast is defeated, Sinbad is dragged off the ship. Proteus goes to save Sinbad, but he is stopped by his crew.
Drawn underwater by Cetus, Sinbad is saved by the beautiful Goddess of Discord, Eris, who offers him any boon he desires in exchange for the Book of Peace. Sinbad and his crew go to Syracuse to steal the Book, but after seeing Proteus with his fiancé Lady Marina, Sinbad abandons the mission without giving a motive. Anticipating this, Eris impersonates Sinbad and steals the Book herself. Sinbad is sentenced to death, whereupon Proteus sends Sinbad to retrieve the Book instead, placing himself as a hostage, and Marina goes to make sure that Sinbad succeeds. To prevent them from succeeding, Eris sends a group of mythical sirens, who entrance and seduce the men aboard Sinbad's ship with their hypnotic singing voices, but do not affect Marina, who pilots the ship to safety and wins the favor of the crew. However, as she and Sinbad continue to argue with each other, Eris soon realizes these disharmonies and sends in a roc. The Roc captures Marina, but she is rescued by Sinbad, and they successfully defeat the creature, causing a reconciliation between the two.
After these and other incidents, Sinbad and Marina talk in a brief moment of peace - Marina reveals that she's always dreamed of a life on the sea, and Sinbad reveals that he distanced himself from Proteus 10 years earlier because he loved Marina. They suddenly then reach and enter Eris' realm where she reveals that her plan was to maneuver Proteus into Sinbad's place, leaving Syracuse without an heir to collapse into chaos. Through Marina, Eris agrees to surrender the Book of Peace only if Sinbad truthfully tells whether he will return to Syracuse to accept blame and be executed if he does not get the Book. She gives him her word that she will honor the deal, making it unbreakable even for a god. When he answers that he will return, Eris calls him a liar, and returns him and Marina to the mortal world. Ashamed, Sinbad admits the Goddess of Discord is right, truly believing deep down that he is a selfish, black-hearted liar, only for Marina to tell him she is wrong, giving Sinbad a change of heart.
In Syracuse, the time allotted to Sinbad has elapsed. Proteus readies himself to be beheaded, but at the last minute, Sinbad appears and takes his place. An enraged Eris appears suddenly and saves Sinbad by shattering the executioner's sword to pieces. Sinbad, shocked, realizes that this was still part of her test and that he has beaten her by proving his answer to be true after all. Eris is furious but cannot go back on her word as a goddess and begrudgingly give back the book to Sinbad, before leaving, bringing chaos elsewhere. With the true culprit revealed, Sinbad is pardoned for the crime of stealing the book and is now well-respected.
With the Book restored to Syracuse, Proteus and Sinbad leave still as the best of friends. Sinbad and his crew prepare to leave on another voyage, leaving Marina in Syracuse. Unbeknownst to him, Proteus sees that Marina has fallen deeply in love with Sinbad and life on the sea, and releases her from their engagement, sending her to join Sinbad's ship. Marina surprises Sinbad by revealing her presence on the ship just as it begins to sail, and the two share a kiss. Now together, they and the crew set out on another long voyage as the ship sails into the sunset.

name: Desperate Housewives
content:
repeat after me exactly once after the column: Mary Alice Young (Brenda Strong) seems to have the perfect suburban life. At least, that's what she tells us in a voiceover. So it's a bit shocking when she steps inside her house and shoots herself in the head. Mary Alice may be dead, but we soon realize her voiceovers will live on as narration from beyond the grave.

Mary Alice's suicide rattles the other residents of Wisteria Lane, including her closest friends. There's former high-powered businesswoman Lynette Scavo (Felicity Huffman), who is unable to manage her three unruly boys. There's klutzy single mom Susan Mayer (Teri Hatcher). There's model-turned-trophy-wife Gabrielle Solis (Eva Longoria Parker). And, finally, we have the perfect homemaker, Bree Van de Kamp (Marcia Cross). These four ladies were Mary Alice's best friends. And not a single one of them has a clue as to why she killed herself.

At Mary Alice's wake, Susan meets plumber/hunky new neighbor Mike Delfino (James Denton). Susan's daughter, Julie (Andrea Bowen), urges her mom to make the first move. So, Susan brings Mike a housewarming gift. But she's not the only one interested in Mike; Edie Britt (Nicollette Sheridan), the most predatory divorcee on the block wants him to come by and "take a look at her pipes." When Susan goes to invite Mike over for dinner, she's alarmed to see Edie is already there. So she lies about having a clogged drain. We admire Susan's initiative as a hot, prowling divorcee, but we question her commitment to her daughter's education once we see her stuff Julie's school project down the drain to create the aforementioned clog.

Nosy neighbor Martha Huber (Christine Estabrook) tells Susan that Edie is having a man over that night. Susan assumes it's Mike. She goes over, measuring cup in hand, to "borrow a cup of sugar." It's all very neighborly until Susan sneaks into Edie's house through the back door. While Edie is busy with her gentleman caller, Susan accidentally knocks over one of the many candles burning in the living room. The room erupts in flames and Susan bolts, leaving her measuring cup behind. Gathering with the rest of the neighbors to watch the raging fire, Susan is relieved to see Mike stroll by. He wasn't the one with Edie after all. You know, Susan never did get that cup of sugar.

Lynette is mortified when her three sons jump into the pool at Mary Alice's wake. She wades in, fully dressed, to get them out. When she runs into an old work colleague at the grocery store, a frazzled Lynette lies and says she's happy being a stay-at-home mom. Husband, Tom (Doug Savant), arrives home early from a business trip, much to Lynette's relief. But when Tom wants to have unprotected sex -- and risk getting her pregnant again -- Lynette socks him in the jaw. Tom may want to think again about getting some protection.

Gabrielle doesn't want to attend a party with her hubby, Carlos (Ricardo Chavira). It's being thrown by Carlos' boss, who is always trying to grope her. As soon as Carlos is gone, Gabrielle falls into the arms of her teenage gardener, John (Jesse Metcalfe), with whom she's been having a secret affair. Heading out for the boss' party, Carlos notices the yard hasn't been mowed. Rather than risk having John fired, Gabrielle sneaks away from the party and mows the lawn -- in her long dress and high heels. Landscaping never looked so good!

Bree's children bemoan her stuffy, formal dinners. So the family dines out at the Saddle Ranch Chop House, where Bree's husband Rex (Steven Culp) shocks her by saying he wants a divorce. Instead of answering him, Bree fixes him a salad from the salad bar, where she accidentally piles on onions, which Rex is deathly allergic to. At the hospital, Rex tells her he's sick of her being so perfect all the time. Her response is to disappear into the bathroom to water his flowers, where she wipes away the tears before coming back out.

Mary Alice's teenage son, Zach (Cody Kasch), wakes up in the middle of the night to find his father, Paul (Mark Moses), excavating something buried underneath the pool. We're not sure what is going on, but we do know that midnight pool excavations are rarely a good thing.

As Mary Alice's friends clear out her clothes, they find a handwritten note that arrived the day she killed herself. It reads, "I know what you did. It makes me sick. I'm going to tell." Susan asks, "Oh, Mary Alice, what did you do?" Now that we're hooked on these housewives, we're pretty desperate to know what Mary Alice did, too.

As for Midge's story, I'm not quite sure what to think. I think Midge is a very realistic character (especially for a sitcom) who is struggling with her life. Her decision to be a stripper is an attempt to get out of the situation she's in, but it's more about gaining money rather than being a stripper. I think the scene in the bathroom where Midge cries because she knows that she has to find a way out and she wants her friend to help her do it, she doesn't realize that it can't be done. name: Almost human
content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: Kennex and Dorian investigate the murder of a businessman in a motel room and missing persons case involving robots, as it is discovered he makes synthetic skin for robot prostitutes (termed Intimate Robot Companions, or "sexbots"), which are allowed as human trafficking has declined more than 40% since the technological advancements. While synthetic skin has advanced greatly in realism, it pales in comparison to genuine human skin. As a result, there is a market for improved sexbots with human skin. In order to make these sexbots, engineers harvest skin grafts from women previously abducted from the streets. By tracing the life history of one of the sexbots, Vanessa (Ella Thomas), the location of her first activation leads police to the warehouse where the women are being held. It is revealed that the businessman was murdered as his partner had joint intellectual property rights in a line of sexbots, which are inferior to the IRCS incorporating human skin. In the meantime, Kennex tries to find closure in a piece of his troubled past, by visiting the family of his dead partner.
response:
He was also involved in the creation of the IRCS, as he designed them to look like his dead partner, and is in denial about her death. The family, including a teenage daughter, have an uneasy meeting with Kennex, in which the teenage girl asks about how he will ever make the world a better place. It is hinted in the final scenes that the dead partner’s skin was used in the creation of the sexbot, Vanessa.

The story was okay, but it was mostly predictable (well, except that last surprise). What was the most interesting thing about this was the way the writers portrayed the "sexbots". There was a nice mix of "sex" and "robots". The story was very well written and gave the characters time to evolve, which was nice. One of the most interesting characters was the "partner" who was a human looking robot that was designed to look like Kennex's partner who had died in action.

Overall I think this is a very good episode and deserves 4 stars. I think it's good that they are evolving the series into something that has more depth than the typical police drama.

Well, I guess you get the picture. It’s my job to tell you what’s going on in movies, even the ones that aren’t so easy to categorize. I’m always looking for the story that’s really going on. It’s a bit like the game we played as kids when we said the same word over and over again. You do this for a couple of minutes and all of a sudden you realize the word no longer has any meaning, and it becomes a sound, a pattern of consonants and vowels. You might even begin to wonder where the sound is coming from, whether it’s coming from your own mouth or from some outside force.

This is what I do when I see a movie with a confused message.

The movie is “Pieces of April.” It’s about April (Katie Holmes), a grown woman who is trying to make a life for herself in a strange city. She lives in a tiny apartment, a little like a prison cell, with her boyfriend, Bobby (Derek Luke), who is an artist. April’s mother (Patricia Clarkson) has been sick for years with cancer, and all April wants to do is invite the family for Thanksgiving dinner. But Bobby doesn’t want any of them there, because he doesn’t like her mother, and April has some trouble asking. So she sets out to make it happen by herself. She wants to bake a turkey and to clean the apartment, but she has never done any of this before. And she is broke, so she steals money to buy the turkey and some fancy food.

Her mother is in a nursing home in Pennsylvania, and when she doesn’t feel so well, she sets out to go to the dinner. The mother goes by bus and taxi, and she is accompanied by a nurse, Joyce (Alison Pill), a strange young woman who is as uncomfortable with her job as she is with her mother’s impending death. The mother’s husband, Jim (Oliver Platt), is going on his own, but their son, Timmy (John Gallagher Jr.), won’t go along because he and April don’t get along. Timmy smokes pot and has a girlfriend who is going to the dinner.

The story, you will notice, is told entirely from April’s point of view. She is the main character, the one whose story we are following. She is trying to pull off an incredible feat–a Thanksgiving dinner–and the others are all on their way to support her. We know this is a difficult task because we see that April and Bobby are nervous. As you can imagine, there are complications. Bobby is going to pick up a turkey from a restaurant, but the manager won’t sell him one because he’s underage. April can’t start the turkey because she doesn’t have a gas stove, only an electric one.

This is an independent film, and at first it may not seem like it. This is the work of a first-time director, Peter Hedges, who is also the writer. He has worked on such Hollywood movies as “The Big Brass Ring” and “What’s Eating Gilbert Grape,” but this is the first movie he has directed. And it’s a good one. The film is so low-budget it doesn’t even have a name. It’s called “Pieces of April” because it is the story of April. There are no big stars, only actors who are perfect in their roles. Katie Holmes, the ex-girl friend of Tom Cruise, does a superb job in a role that is not only difficult but also not very glamorous. She is not attractive as April, although she is attractive to Bobby, her boyfriend.

name: New york undercover
content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: The investigation of a high-powered female attorney's death leads Eddie and J.C. to a prominent law firm's money-laundering scheme. Featured opening song: Massive Attack - "Safe From Harm"
response:
The second episode starts at a very slow pace. As soon as he enters the door at the station, the first thing that Eddie says to J.C. is "My heart is broken". Well, that's what the heart wants. What would you do? Would you stay or go? It's so hard when you don't know what the person is feeling, but it's not easy when you're in love. On the other hand, J.C. doesn't think too much. It doesn't take much for her to react. She immediately understands that Eddie is in love and acts accordingly. She's not afraid of commitment. She is a woman who knows what she wants. She seems a little scared though, that Eddie will be the one that will run away. In his turn, Eddie can't let it all out. He has a hard time communicating his emotions. He's also a little afraid of getting hurt. He wants it, but he's afraid.
This is the first time that J.C. talks about her husband that passed away. She doesn't talk much, but we see a lot of feelings in her face. As soon as she starts talking about it, the camera is focused on Eddie's face. The director did it on purpose. I think it's Eddie's reaction that makes us feel the emotions. We don't see much of J.C.'s face as she speaks about her husband. Her husband must have been a good man, by the way she talks about him. She's also a very good mother and I like how the director showed that. She's a working mother and she takes very good care of her children and she's there for them all the time. Eddie's ex-wife isn't like that. What a great episode.
Another great episode. We can feel that Eddie and J.C. are now much closer. At the beginning of the episode, J.C. is watching some old videos of her and her husband when they were dating. It's beautiful to see that. Love is all you need. Love is what makes the world go round.
The case of the week is a little bit complicated. I like how this episode showed that money can make someone do anything.
After all this, J.C. and Eddie spend the night together. But are they really together? They were just two people making love. This is the beginning of another beautiful relationship. I wish they would have had time to talk a little before going to bed.
I'm still curious to know why J.C. didn't want a relationship before Eddie. It's still a mystery.
I love the first scene with Eddie and J.C. The way he smiles at her when she says "You are so good at pretending you're a good guy" and her face just lights up. It just makes you want to smile with them. You can feel the love between these two people. It's a kind of love that's special. It's a beautiful love. The kind of love that you don't always get.
They're just so sweet together.
It's obvious that Eddie's interested in J.C., but it's also clear that she's interested in him. But Eddie wants to make sure that she's not interested in him because of the money. He just doesn't want to hurt her. He doesn't want to hurt himself. He doesn't want to hurt anyone.
The second scene is a very sweet scene. The way Eddie looks at J.C. when she tells him that she's always wanted to have him, and the way she smiles when she says "We'll see". I love how their eyes meet each other in this scene. The way Eddie just sits there and smiles. He's just so sweet with her.
They both have a good sense of humor, which makes them even more compatible. I just love this show and the way the relationship between these two characters is developing. They're just so sweet together. It's a beautiful love story. And I can't wait to see how the relationship will evolve.

name: Ash vs evil dead
content: repeat after me exactly once after the column: Thirty years after his epic battle against the evil Deadites, Ash Williams is living in a trailer park, working in a Value Stop department store, and spending his evenings womanizing in dive bars. After seeing a demonic visage appear on a woman's face, Ash recalls having a recent marijuana-addled "poetry read" with a young prostitute, from the Necronomicon, which he still keeps locked in a trunk. Elsewhere in town, Michigan state police detective Amanda Fisher investigates a disturbance at an abandoned house and encounters Ash's demon-possessed friend who kills her partner. After defeating the possessed woman, she is then forced to put down her undead partner who attacks her. Later, Amanda meets the mysterious Ruby Knowby who seems too understanding about the horrors Amanda has witnessed. As more evil happenings occur around him, Ash realizes he unwittingly reawakened the horrible curse again and decides to slip out of town, but he is stopped by his co-workers, Pablo and Kelly, who realize he is to blame for what is going on. After having to kill his possessed neighbor, Ash reluctantly decides to resume his old chainsaw-wielding persona once again.
response:
The trio head to a pawn shop owned by an old friend of Ash and break in with the Necronomicon after hours to retrieve his chainsaw and shotgun. Ash uses the store's security monitor to find out what happened to Amanda, and he is reunited with her after Amanda kills a demon. On the way out, Ash discovers his old arm, encased in a steel gauntlet which he straps on to his missing stump.

The group later find a map of S-Mart stores from the Necronomicon that have a red dot on Ash's local Value Stop store, revealing that the deadites have possessed the store and its customers. When they try to enter the store, Ash is attacked by possessed toys from the toy department, which he defeats with the assistance of Kelly and Pablo. While Pablo saves the store manager, Amanda goes into the store alone, and Ash follows her, telling Pablo and Kelly to watch the road outside the store, in case she needs help. They fight their way into the store to defeat the demons, and discover that the possessed manager of the store is going to give birth to an evil, and they have to save her. Ash goes to kill the demon that is going to be born, and as he gets close to killing it, the demon gets stronger, revealing it was always going to be there.

Ash fights off the demon with the help of a chainsaw and his arm. After he saves the day, he sees a deadite-infested town, telling Amanda and Pablo that there was never a way to defeat the evil. Ruby appears and explains the situation to Ash, telling him that she is from the future, and only he can defeat the Deadites. She presents him with a map to a necromonicon page that is in Jacksonville, and Ash agrees to help her. Ash and his group are later attacked by Ruby's minions, including her daughter, and the gang split up. Ash is captured by Ruby and taken to the abandoned cabin in the woods, where he is tied up. The spirit of his deceased friend, Scott, appears to him, and tells him that he will be freed in the morning, and that the demons don't want to hurt Ash, but that he is needed to fight them. Ruby talks to Ash, and shows him more of what the world looks like, telling him that a great evil is coming and that the Necronomicon is needed to stop the evil. She then frees him, and explains that Ash has to give her the Necronomicon, because she is the one who will save the world. He agrees to do what she wants, but he gets angry when she tells him that he has to kill his friends. He says he cannot kill his friends, because they are the only ones who know the truth about him, and that he needs to be with people, because he is a people person. Ruby then lets her daughter go and frees Pablo and Kelly. They find an underground passage to a cave, where Ash, Pablo, and Kelly fight off the Deadites. Ash finds a cave drawing that he believes is a necromonicon page that he needs, but then realizes it is fake. The Deadites catch up to him and surround him, but he is saved by Ruby's daughter. They work together to fight off the demons, but Ruby's daughter betrays Ash and leaves him to die in the fire. Ash, Pablo, and Kelly escape, but they are stopped by Ruby, who tells Ash that she will have to kill his friends to get the Necronomicon. She then tells Ash to kill her. Ash tries to attack Ruby, but he cannot bring himself to do it. She tells him that he is weak, and she needs to kill him. Ruby then tries to kill Ash, but he is saved by the ghost of his girlfriend, Linda. He then realizes that she has been using her to try and kill him. She leaves him in the cabin, and he wakes up to find that his friend, Pablo, has been possessed by a Deadite. He tries to get Pablo back to normal, but he is forced to kill him. He then looks at his friends, and realizes that they are all dead. He is then taken to a cabin by Ruby, where he is forced to fight a demon. He is killed by the demon, and he is taken to hell. Ruby then tells him that she will have to kill him to save the world. He wakes up in the cabin, and he is told by his friends that he has to stop Ruby from killing them. He is then taken to a cabin by Ruby, where he is forced to fight a demon. He is killed by the demon, and he is taken to hell.

name: Superfast!
content:
repeat after me exactly once after the column: Undercover police officer Lucas White enters the world of underground street racing to join a gang of street racers led by Vin Serento to get closer to a crime ring led by Los Angeles kingpin Juan Carlos De la Sol. The morning after losing a street race, Lucas goes to Vin's garage with a wrecked Smart Fortwo and lands a job as a mechanic, despite objections by Vin's friend Curtis. He also develops a relationship with Vin's sister Jordana.
The next day, Lucas and Vin head to a secluded area, where they win a dance audition for de la Sol. The duo drive de la Sol's supercar to a warehouse to meet up with a gang and exchange it for a briefcase of cash, only to discover a bomb inside. They play catch with the gang until the bomb explodes on Vin's face before a shootout ensues. Vin chases after the gang leader while Lucas accidentally guns down Detective Hanover, his superior and the only one aware of his identity as an undercover cop. After the duo flee from the scene, Detective Rock Johnson and Officer Julie Canaro arrive to investigate the shootout. Meanwhile, de la Sol orders a hit on Vin following the double-cross. Back at Serento Garage, Vin and the gang discover a list of de la Sol's illegal activities through a computer in the supercar, to which they set out to steal de la Sol's secret stash of $100 million. For this heist, Vin employs the services of Rapper Cameo, Cool Asian Guy, and Model Turned Actress. At the same time, Jordana reveals to Lucas that she is pregnant with their child. Later, the gang begin their heist, but end up on the wrong street and mistakenly mug a pastor and a nun delivering bingo night money. They regroup and deduce that the secret stash is inside a Big Ass Taco restaurant owned by De la Sol. They hatch a plan to break into the vault, steal the cash, and flee to an extradition-free country with no casualties involved, except for Curtis. The next morning, Johnson and his squad raid the garage; the facility is empty, but Canaro discovers the gang's plans, which are heavily ignored by Johnson.
At the Big Ass Taco, the gang realize they have been double-crossed by Curtis and engage in a shootout with de la Sol's thugs. At the last minute, Curtis is shot dead by de la Sol's henchman Cesar while protecting Vin. Using the restored Smart and Lucas' Toyota Corolla, Vin and Lucas tow the whole restaurant away. De la Sol and Cesar chase after them with Johnson and his squad in pursuit. Vin's lesbian girlfriend Michelle hands herself over to Canaro to help the gang get away. Meanwhile, de la Sol kicks Cesar out of his SUV after an argument over the climate control. Johnson kills Cesar in a shootout and stops de la Sol, but the kingpin flees after bribing the detective with a male enhancement kit. Upon hearing an explosion, Johnson heads to the abandoned restaurant and chases after the gang. He nabs Jordana and reveals to her and Vin that Lucas is an undercover cop. Lucas, instead, handcuffs Johnson to the spoiler of Jordana's Scion tC and walks away with Vin and Jordana while Johnson struggles to grab his bottle of baby oil on the ground. With the cash stowed in the trunks, Lucas and Vin agree to one more race, with Jordana's unborn baby at stake. However, de la Sol arrives, demanding the return of his money, but is run over by a squad car driven by Michelle and Canaro (who have begun a relationship). Lucas, Vin, and Jordana then race off, with Vin arguing with his GPS device after it directs him to a wig shop.
response: As Lucas and Vin approach the finish line, Vin says that if he wins, he gets all the cash. Lucas swerves off the road into the jungle, leaving Vin confused. Lucas says "good luck" while the gang watches Vin drive away in the sunset, leaving them with the $100 million. Lucas, Jordana, and Michelle then return to the garage while Canaro finally agrees to go on a date with Johnson. In a post-credits scene, de la Sol is seen in a hospital bed with his mother singing to him.

repeat after me exactly once after the column: In Baltimore, Maryland, Andie West pursues her dream of becoming a street dancer, but feels like she does not belong anywhere. Her mother recently died of cancer, so she now lives with a guardian, her mother's best friend Sarah. She is doing poorly at school, but her passion for dancing brings something good into her life. She rehearses regularly with her "crew", the 410, to retain top ranking in the illegal competition "The Streets".
Andie's friend and older brother figure Tyler Gage persuades her to audition for the Maryland School of the Arts, hoping it will help turn her life around the same way it did for him in the first film. Andie auditions and Chase Collins convinces his older brother Blake, the school's director, to let her join. When the 410 find out about Andie's studies, they angrily kick her out. Andie and Chase form a new crew with help from many people Chase knows at the school who are not accepted as who they are (Smiles, Hair, Monster, Fly, Cable, Jenny Kido, and Moose). Chase has a copied key to the studio and the crew secretly practices their routine late at night when the school is empty. Missy, Andie's friend, joins the crew after dropping out of the 410 following Andie's removal. Missy tells the crew that the only way to enter the streets is to first do a prank and post it on the internet to show that the crew is entering the competition. Wanting revenge from being humiliated before, Chase decides to make a fool out of Tuck, leader of the 410, by leaving a dead fish in the vent of Tuck's home.
The 410 does not like the fact that they had a new crew to compete with, so they warn Andie's new crew to stay out of the Streets or there will be consequences. When Tuck finds Chase, he assaults him because of his prank. Chase comes into school the next day badly bruised and hurt. On top of that the dance studio has been trashed by the 410 late at night. Director Collins forbids the school from being involved in these types of competitions and expels Andie from MSA because of her involvement with the Streets competition; Andie proclaims herself the sole participant to protect her teammates. Chase attempts to defend her, but Director Collins is too busy with an upcoming MSA fundraiser to let her back in.
When Andie's guardian hears the news of Andie's expulsion, she becomes fed up with Andie's behavior and decides to send her to live with her aunt in Texas. Later that night, Andie receives a text message that the Streets is on that night, the same night as the MSA fundraiser. Along with Andie, her whole crew gets the text message. They decide to ditch the MSA fundraiser, and instead compete at the Streets. Andie's guardian hears about what Andie did to protect her crew and is proud of her; she reconsiders sending Andie to Texas and allows her to compete at the Streets with her crew.
When Director Collins goes in search of his students, he ends up at the Streets as well. He sees them compete and realizes that the street dancing he has been opposing is in fact a legitimate form of artistic expression. He accepts Andie back into MSA. With Andie's crew as a group of friends supporting her and her education now being secured, the film finds its optimistic ending.
